content:
emily (acct): Heads up 1: CatalystBank sent an RFP asking for a 10-day POC. Requirements: private deploy in their AWS account, FIPS 140-2 HSM integration, 45ms p95 latency target (short chat), and a 12-month committed pricing schedule. They also want an exec one-pager capability matrix + a plain-language key-custody line. Can we triage today?

jiro (solutions): Quick triage: NDA first. Main risks: HSM wiring for onprem/cloud, latency depends heavily on peak RPS and token lengths, and we should offer an appliance option for sensitive offices.

olga (eng): 45ms p95 for ~32-token replies is doable with redwood-13B int8 on Dedicated A10s colocated in their region. If they want multi-region failover or KV-heavy contexts latency will increase. Need expected QPS and typical prompt lengths. For HSM: we support KMIP + CloudHSM; on-prem HSM needs a reachable KMIP endpoint and allowed ports.

ben (security): Key custody: for Private and appliance deployments, customer maintains keys. Draft blurb: "Customer retains exclusive custody of cryptographic keys. Redwood stores only encrypted key references and does not have access to plaintext key material." I'll add to the RFI appendix.

emily (acct): POC commercial ask: they want a transient POC rate and committed tiers. Any rule-of-thumb for POC discount and GPU buckets?

jiro (solutions): Typical POC: 40-50% off committed list for up to 14 days, cap 8 GPUs. Committed tiers: small=4, mid=16, large=64. I'll prepare a short CSV with per-GPU monthly list and committed discounts.

olga (eng): I'll draft a one-page capability matrix with rows: redwood-7B/13B/70B + appliance-70B. Columns: quant (fp16/int8/int4), p95 latency (32/64 tokens), throughput/GPU or appliance, and $/token rough (committed vs burst). Example row: "redwood-13B | int8 | 36ms p95 (32t) | 120 req/s per A10 | $0.0009/token (committed)"

ben (security): Also request their compliance prompt set (PII examples) so we can run redaction and hallucination tests during POC. We'll need an NDA before they share that.

emily (acct): Can we turn around the one-pager + pricing CSV + RFI appendix by EOD PST? Customer asked for an exec summary to share with their procurement committee.

jiro (solutions): Yes. I'll draft pricing + POC terms now. Olga  can you include a short caveat line: "Latency estimates assume Dedicated capacity in-region and typical cache-hit rates; actual p95 depends on prompt distribution" for execs?

olga (eng): Yep. Also I'll include a tiny eval note: run both int8 and fp16 on their critical prompt-set to validate quality vs latency. Snippet: ```bash
# run perf
python eval.py --config=int8 --prompts=customer_prompts.json
```

ops-bot: Ticket #POC-7831 created and assigned to emily, jiro, olga. Due 2024-11-14.

emily (acct): I'll request NDA and HSM contact + VPC CIDR + allowed ports + expected peak RPS + sample prompts in handoff email. Once NDA is signed we can schedule kickoff. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
